themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints surged to 55 THIS WEEK versus 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 577% spike (z-score: 5.38)—suggesting acute pavement, pothole, or sidewalk deterioration affecting multiple blocks in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights.
evidence: Street Condition complaints: 55 THIS WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly baseline (z-score 5.38, severity high)
CB budget requests repeatedly ask for sanitation trucks and equipment from DSNY, indicating chronic underfunding
367 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days, mostly alterations (324), suggesting heavy construction activity may be degrading streets
reporting_angles: Conduct block-by-block visual survey of reported street damage; interview residents about safety hazards
Request DSNY repair timeline and staffing data to explain why infrastructure complaints are spiking now

themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints exploded to 7 LAST WEEK versus 0.2 weekly average—a 2700% spike (z-score: 15.59, severity high)—indicating severe sanitation service breakdown across the district.
evidence: Missed Collection: 7 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score 15.59, severity high)
CB repeatedly requests funding for additional sanitation trucks and equipment from DSNY—unfunded need persisting across budget cycles
Spike is statistically extreme (z-score 15.59), indicating this is not normal variance
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about staffing shortages, truck breakdowns, or route changes affecting Morningside/Hamilton Heights
Document resident complaints about uncollected refuse and health/pest risks; photograph accumulation sites

themes_detail.label: Pest & Animal Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Two converging pest spikes THIS WEEK: Unsanitary Animal Pvt Property jumped 1900% (5 complaints vs. 0.2 avg) and Dead Animal complaints surged 1100% last week (3 vs. 0.2 avg), alongside persistent Rodent complaints UP 173% (14 last week vs. 5.1 avg), suggesting public health crisis.
evidence: Unsanitary Animal Pvt Property: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score 10.97, severity high)
Dead Animal: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score 6.35, severity high)
Rodent: 14 complaints last week vs. 5.1 weekly average (z-score 6.11, severity high)
CB budget requests animal/pest control and rat reduction as recurring, unfunded priority from DOHMH
Convergence: three pest-related categories spiking simultaneously within 2-week window suggests systemic failure
reporting_angles: Investigate why dead animals and pest complaints are clustering now—possible food source, sanitation gap, or seasonal pattern
Interview DOHMH and local health department about rodent abatement efforts and whether missed trash collection is driving infestation
Profile residents in affected blocks; document health and safety concerns, especially for elderly and immunocompromised

themes_detail.label: Building Inspection Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Two city inspection agencies spiked THIS WEEK: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped 700% (4 vs. 0.5 avg) and OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints surged 567% (5 vs. 0.8 avg), alongside Emergency Response Team activity up 2300% last week—suggesting unannounced enforcement actions or structural/safety concerns.
evidence: Special Projects Inspection Team: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score 7.0, severity high)
OUTSIDE BUILDING: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score 6.43, severity high)
Emergency Response Team: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score 8.69, severity high)
Convergence of three city agency complaints within same 2-week window suggests coordinated response or multiple incidents
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with FDNY and Buildings Department for incident reports and violations issued in Morningside/Hamilton Heights this week
Identify which buildings/addresses triggered SPIT and ERT activity; determine if related to 1727 Amsterdam Avenue (Hill Top Apartments ULURP) or other construction

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Complaints Remain Chronic
themes_detail.summary: Heat and Hot Water complaints total 5,191 over 90 days—by far the largest complaint category—reflecting a persistent, structural housing code violation issue, though no acute spike detected THIS WEEK, indicating chronic rather than emergency condition.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water: 5,191 complaints over 90 days—largest complaint category by far
No statistical spike detected this week, indicating endemic, long-running problem rather than emergency
Pattern suggests systemic landlord non-compliance with heat season obligations (likely Oct–May)
reporting_angles: Profile 3–4 households living without adequate heat; document health impacts and tenant remedies available
Obtain HPD enforcement data: how many violations issued, how many buildings repeat violators, what is average time to repair
